title: PACHA Malware Investigation
description: Investigate and respond to a PACHA malware infection on Linux servers.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The scenario simulates a network compromised by the PACHA backdoor malware, which is known to infect Linux servers with coinminers. The malware uses iptables rules and downloads additional payloads from various URLs. Your task is to investigate the compromised hosts, identify the malware's persistence mechanisms, and contain the threat. The learning objective is to understand the lifecycle of a malware compromise, from initial access to data exfiltration, and to apply appropriate incident response techniques. This includes initial access, persistence, lateral movement, and data exfiltration.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) via SSH using the provided credentials.
levels.local_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) via SSH using the provided credentials.

levels.title: Identify the Suspicious Service
levels.content: The compromised host is communicating with a command and control server. Investigate the running services and identify the suspicious service used for C2 communication. The flag is the name of the suspicious service used for C2 communication.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual services. The suspicious service used for C2 communication is sh.service.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd services are used to manage system processes. Look for any unusual or unfamiliar services.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service' to list all running services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The suspicious service name starts with 'sh'.

levels.title: Investigate the Service Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: The malware has established persistence on the compromised host. Investigate the service persistence mechanism and identify the service name. The flag is the name of the service used for persistence.
levels.solution: Check the systemd services and look for any unusual services. The service name used for persistence is sh.service.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Persistence mechanisms often involve systemd services that start automatically at boot.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service' to list all running services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The service name used for persistence is the same as the suspicious service identified in the previous task.

levels.title: Contain the C2 Communication
levels.content: To prevent further communication with the command and control server, you need to block the outbound port used for C2 communication. Identify the port number used for C2 communication. The flag is the port number used for C2 communication.
levels.solution: Check the listening ports and look for any unusual ports. The port number used for C2 communication is 80. Block it using iptables.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Command and control communication often occurs over common ports used for web traffic.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'ss -tulnp' to list all listening ports.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The port number used for C2 communication is 80.
